Senses.Explanation: The records warn against collapsing into blank nothing, then answer that blankness itself is absent or is not blank. Literally, 'fall into emptiness,' but in these records the observable warning is against falling into a blank nothing. The term occurs 325 times in 128 allowed texts; the expanded form 'fall into blank annihilation' (落空亡) occurs 63 times in 37 texts. Dahui reports people who hear 'a teaching in which nothing is obtained' (無所得法) and become afraid that they will fall into blankness; he answers by asking whether the very one who fears falling into blankness is empty. A lamp dialogue answers the charge that Chan teachers mostly fall into blankness by saying that letters and other things arise from wisdom and that, when 'great function appears before one' (大用現前), there can be no falling into blankness. Another exchange dismantles the spatial wording itself: asked whether 'originally there is nothing' falls into blankness, the reply asks, 'Since blankness is absent, from where could falling be established?' (空既是無，墮從何立). The same collection says that people fear forgetting mind because they fear falling into blankness with nowhere to get hold, then says 'blankness itself is originally not blank' (空本無空). There are 37 occurrences of 'not fall into blankness' (不落空) and 21 of the warning 'do not fall into blankness' (莫落空).
Senses.Note: The translation 'blankness' follows the records' direct corrections: 'Since blankness is absent, from where could falling be established?' (空既是無，墮從何立), and 'blankness itself is originally not blank' (空本無空). The entry records the corpus's accusations, warnings, and replies.

Occurrences.Kwic: 纔聞善知識說無所得法。便心裏疑惑。怕落空去。妙喜每見如此說者。即問他。只這怕落空者。還空也無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (大慧普覺禪師語錄). Dahui describes the fear and responds by questioning whether the one who fears falling into blankness is itself empty. The exact headword-bearing actor is Dahui Zonggao.

Occurrences.Kwic: 古德喚作落空亡外道魂不散死人。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source text (大慧普覺禪師語錄). Dahui cites an older description: 'an outsider fallen into blank annihilation, a dead person whose ghost has not dispersed.' The exact headword-bearing actor is Dahui Zonggao.

Occurrences.Kwic: 有律師法明。謂師曰。禪師家多落空。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Transmission of the Lamp (景德傳燈錄): the named Vinaya lecturer Faming directly states that Chan teachers mostly fall into blankness; Dazhu Huihai is the respondent.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: Faming’s clause 謂師曰 is declarative direct speech: the named Vinaya lecturer tells Dazhu Huihai that Chan teachers mostly fall into blankness; Dazhu replies in the next turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰本來無莫落空否。師曰。空既是無墮從何立。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: (景德傳燈錄). The exact actor is an unnamed Chan visitor: he asks (本來無莫落空否). No personal name remains after the six-rung review.
